title: The Archive of Ordinary Voices
title_ja: 日常の声を集めた資料館
fact_notes: 人物・制度・具体的な出来事は架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A small fictional town decided to create an archive of recordings about the history of its railway station.
sentences.ja: 架空の小さな町は鉄道駅の歴史について録音資料館を作ることにした。

sentences.en: The organizers initially invited former station managers to describe important changes to the building and its services.
sentences.ja: 主催者は最初、元駅長たちに建物やサービスの重要な変化を説明するよう求めた。

sentences.en: Their accounts provided useful information about official decisions, but one volunteer wondered whose experiences were still absent from the collection.
sentences.ja: その話は公式決定について有益な情報を提供したが、ある協力者は誰の経験がまだ資料に欠けているか疑問に思った。

sentences.en: She suggested interviewing passengers, cleaning staff, and people who had operated shops near the station.
sentences.ja: 乗客、清掃職員、駅の近くで店を営んだ人への聞き取りを提案した。

sentences.en: One retired cleaner remembered changes in the daily routine that were rarely mentioned in official announcements.
sentences.ja: 引退した清掃員は公式告知ではめったに触れられない日常業務の変化を覚えていた。

sentences.en: A shopkeeper described how the introduction of a new entrance affected the number of people walking past her store.
sentences.ja: 店主は新しい入口の導入が店の前を歩く人の数にどう影響したか説明した。

sentences.en: Other interviewees recalled experiences connected with family visits, school journeys, or unexpected delays during severe weather.
sentences.ja: 他の聞き取り対象者は家族訪問、通学、悪天候での予期しない遅延に関わる経験を思い出した。

sentences.en: These accounts did not necessarily contradict the managers' descriptions, but they revealed aspects of the station that the first interviews had not addressed.
sentences.ja: これらの話は駅長の記述と必ずしも矛盾しなかったが、最初の聞き取りが扱わなかった側面を明らかにした。

sentences.en: The volunteers recognized that inviting a greater variety of people would not automatically produce a complete record of the past.
sentences.ja: より多様な人を招いても自動的に過去の完全な記録ができるわけではないと認識した。

sentences.en: Some former residents could not be contacted, and others did not wish to make their personal memories publicly accessible.
sentences.ja: 連絡できない元住民もいれば個人的記憶の公開を望まない人もいた。

sentences.en: Even among willing participants, recollections of the same incident sometimes differed in details that were difficult to verify.
sentences.ja: 協力的な参加者の間でも、同じ出来事の記憶が確認困難な細部で異なることがあった。

sentences.en: The archive therefore documented when interviews took place and distinguished personal testimony from information confirmed by surviving records.
sentences.ja: そこで聞き取り時期を記録し個人の証言と残存資料で確認した情報を区別した。

sentences.en: For a public exhibition, the organizers selected several short recordings and displayed them alongside maps, photographs, and timetables from different years.
sentences.ja: 公開展示のため短い録音をいくつか選び、異なる年の地図、写真、時刻表と並べた。

sentences.en: They also explained how contributors had been invited and identified some limitations in the range of voices represented.
sentences.ja: 協力者の募集方法も説明し、代表された声の範囲の限界も示した。

sentences.en: Visitors were encouraged to suggest additional questions rather than assume that the exhibition was the final account of the station's history.
sentences.ja: 展示が駅史の最終記述だと考えず、追加の問いを提案するよう来館者に促した。

sentences.en: This approach made the exhibition an invitation to further investigation instead of a claim that every relevant experience had been preserved.
sentences.ja: この方法で展示はすべての関連経験を保存したという主張ではなく、さらなる調査への誘いとなった。

sentences.en: The fictional archive illustrates how historical understanding depends partly on decisions about whose experiences are considered worth recording.
sentences.ja: 架空の資料館は歴史理解が誰の経験に記録する価値があると判断するかにも左右されることを示す。

sentences.en: A wider collection of voices can reveal previously unnoticed questions, although it cannot remove the need to examine the reliability of each source.
sentences.ja: 幅広い声を集めると見落とされていた問いが明らかになるが、各資料の信頼性の確認は必要である。

sentences.en: The challenge is to make historical inquiry more inclusive without treating every recollection as equally accurate or complete.
sentences.ja: 課題はすべての記憶を同等に正確・完全とせず歴史研究をより包摂的にすることだ。

sentences.en: A richer archive gives both answers and reasons to keep asking questions.
sentences.ja: より豊かな資料館は答えと問い続ける理由の双方を提供する。

questions.prompt: Why did the volunteer suggest more interviewees?
options: The managers had given no useful information.
Official accounts omitted some kinds of experience.
questions.explanation_ja: 公式記録にない経験もある。

options: How a new entrance affected pedestrian traffic.

questions.prompt: How did the new accounts relate to earlier ones?
options: They proved all official information false.
They revealed additional aspects without necessarily contradicting them.
Some people could not be contacted or did not want publication.

questions.prompt: Why document interview dates and evidence types?
options: To make every memory automatically correct.
To publish private information without permission.
To distinguish personal accounts from independently confirmed information.
To remove all uncertainty from history.
questions.explanation_ja: 証言と確認資料を区別。

options: The exhibition was not a complete final history.
The organizers wanted visitors to ignore all sources.
The archive had never interviewed anyone.
All historical questions had been solved.
Including a wider range of people or experiences.
Broader historical perspectives should be combined with careful source evaluation.
Official accounts should always be discarded.
All personal memories are equally reliable.
A single exhibition can preserve every experience.
questions.explanation_ja: 多様な視点と資料の吟味。

grammar.explanation_ja: whoseは疑問詞で誰の経験かを表す。
not necessarilyは必ずしも〜しない。

paraphrases.source: Their accounts provided useful information about official decisions, but one volunteer wondered whose experiences were still absent from the collection.
paraphrases.rewrite: Although the managers' accounts helped, the volunteer asked which people's stories had not yet been collected.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 欠けている声を考える。

paraphrases.source: These accounts did not necessarily contradict the managers' descriptions, but they revealed aspects of the station that the first interviews had not addressed.
paraphrases.rewrite: The new accounts could add perspectives without conflicting with the managers' descriptions.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 新たな視点は必ずしも矛盾しない。

paraphrases.source: Even among willing participants, recollections of the same incident sometimes differed in details that were difficult to verify.
paraphrases.rewrite: Even participants who agreed to interviews sometimes remembered hard-to-check details differently.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 確認困難な詳細が異なった。

paraphrases.source: A wider collection of voices can reveal previously unnoticed questions, although it cannot remove the need to examine the reliability of each source.
paraphrases.rewrite: More voices can raise new questions, but individual source reliability still needs scrutiny.
